scope: approval argument binding and atomic consumption
data classification, redaction, retention, and deletion
ownership receipt, backup, update, and complete-removal safety
Phase 1 evaluation safety and preregistration gates

reviewers.focus: authority, privacy, approval, evaluation, and lifecycle adversarial review
schema, semantic-checker, generated-type, chronology, and malformed-input review
invariant ownership, policy extraction, lifecycle proof, and exit-gate review

findings.summary: Committed lifecycle phases originally lacked exact entry, config, and backup coverage.
findings.resolution: The checker derives exact operation-specific target sets, rejects empty proxy rows, and has hash-consistent coverage-gap fixtures.

findings.summary: A nonempty entry or backup target could physically equal its declared root.
findings.resolution: Resource descent is strict, immediate parents are path- and ancestry-bound, and equal-root fixtures reject the alias.

findings.summary: The first receipt proof design compared update preconditions with intended post-state and could not prove absence.
findings.resolution: StateProof/v2 separates preconditions and postconditions, binds update/uninstall to an externally resolved prior receipt, and anchors absence to an exact live parent.

findings.summary: State-proof timestamps did not enforce causal order.
findings.resolution: The checker requires precondition no later than postcondition, postcondition no later than its row, and cross-row proof monotonicity.

findings.summary: Duplicate restoration-purpose backups could suppress an exact restored-target postcondition.
findings.resolution: Each replaced entry and present prior config file has exactly one purpose-matching restoration backup; duplicate fixtures reject ambiguity.

findings.summary: Inherited backups could be changed or dropped despite a valid prior-receipt digest.
findings.resolution: Update/uninstall compare immutable inherited backup projections with the predecessor, permit only the typed restoration transition, and derive restoration proof from prior backup records.

findings.summary: A malformed StateProof could abort semantic fixture validation after the schema had rejected it.
findings.resolution: Semantic proof checks now type-guard malformed proof values and the exact malformed-input fixture completes without a crash.

challenged_suggestions.summary: Persist raw approval arguments in every approval record.
challenged_suggestions.reason: The approved privacy boundary deliberately persists a canonical digest and protected locator while compare-and-consume checks authenticated transient live arguments.

challenged_suggestions.summary: Remove every non-retained entry after uninstall restoration.
challenged_suggestions.reason: A displaced-user entry becomes user-owned when restored and must be excluded from owned-entry removal or the uninstall would delete the restored content.

challenged_suggestions.summary: Require result acceptance to occur after worker termination.
challenged_suggestions.reason: The contract requires result acceptance, terminal state, and verification before unit completion but intentionally permits result submission before worker cleanup ends.
